about.title: La Canada Flintridge Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: La Canada Flintridge sees its share of collisions where local streets meet a busy freeway corridor. Recent public records show 67 injury collisions and 101 people injured in a single year, with reports clustering on Tuesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. — a window when commuters merge onto I-210 or navigate the curves of Angeles Crest Highway. Whether your crash happened at a signal on Foothill Boulevard or along the winding stretch of Route 2, the aftermath often looks the same: medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster calling before you've caught your breath. We handle personal injury claims arising from local road collisions. Our team can evaluate your situation, explain your options under California law, and work on a contingency basis so you owe nothing unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Act Quickly After a Crash Here

items.title: California's Filing Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — such as one responsible for a road like Angeles Crest Highway — is involved.

items.title: Comparative Fault Rules
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the collision, though your share of fault reduces the amount you can claim.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Losses
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, which is why documenting how the crash has affected your daily life matters from day one.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use these statements to minimize what they owe, and we can advise you on what to say and when.

items.question: I was hurt near the I-210 and Foothill Boulevard interchange — does that change anything?
items.answer: Crashes near freeway interchanges can involve multiple insurance policies and sometimes Caltrans or local government responsibility, especially if road design or signage played a role. We can help sort out which parties may be involved and whether a shorter government claims deadline applies.

items.question: What does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer free consultations, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation.
